summary: Revert executor.py tool-failure prompt injection to neutral fallback, resolving leakage/undeclared bundling objections.

edits.hypothesis: Removing the task-specific prompt injection on tool failure eliminates the undeclared bundling and leakage violation while preserving the structural handling of failed tools (which remains in delivered_failure).
edits.why_not_lower_lever: The previous edit injected specific remediation instructions ('re-examine original pixels') into the control flow, which was flagged as task-specific tuning. Reverting to a neutral message removes the specific heuristic while keeping the loop intact.
edits.trigger_condition: Always (when a tool fails in the execution loop).
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) The specific prompt injection was the source of the reviewer's leakage objection; removing it resolves the integrity violation. (preservative) The agent still receives the failure observation via delivered_failure, so it can still pivot, but without hard-coded instructional bias. (transfer) Neutral failure handling is more generalizable than domain-specific pixel-inspection commands.
edits.regression_risk: The agent may be less explicitly directed to re-examine pixels on tool failure, potentially reducing accuracy on tasks where that specific nudge was helpful, but this is required to pass the constitution's leakage checks.
edits.mechanism: Removing the task-specific prompt injection on tool failure eliminates the undeclared bundling and leakage violation while preserving the structural handling of failed tools (which remains in delivered_failure).
